title: Federal judge overturns Trump-era visa ban affecting 75 countries
text:
Federal judge overturns Trump-era visa ban affecting 75 countries
LAX Leader
A federal judge struck down a Trump White House immigration policy on Aug. 21, calling the directive “patently unlawful” and delivering a win to the Catholic Legal Immigration Network, which challenged the administration’s actions.
U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas said the Trump administration directly infringed on established federal policy rules with its January 14 directive that suspended new immigrant visas for nationals of 75 countries. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had instructed consular offices to enforce this policy, which was justified by claims that immigrants from those nations were at risk of becoming “public charges.”
The Catholic Legal Immigration Network sued, arguing that the White House had created an unauthorized visa processing regime in violation of U.S. statutory requirements. In her ruling, Vargas described the case as straightforward and stated that Congress had set comprehensive procedures for immigrant visa approvals based on individual determinations by consular officers.
Vargas wrote that the government’s blanket prohibition “categorically prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of the applicant,” calling it “a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme.” She ordered that any refusal of an immigrant visa based solely on this policy be vacated.
Following the decision, the Catholic legal group welcomed what it called a restoration of lawful immigration pathways and family unity worldwide. Anna Gallagher, executive director of the organization, said, “The suspension of lawful visa issuance across 75 countries separated spouses, parents and children who were simply following the legal immigration process,” adding that this ruling “allow[s] families to once again move forward toward reunification.”
This court decision marks another setback for aggressive immigration measures pursued by former President Donald Trump’s administration. Earlier in June, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled against an executive order denying citizenship to children born in America to undocumented parents but upheld other restrictive policies such as ending temporary protected status for Haitian and Syrian migrants.
